sections.overview: Pasites maculatus is a brood-parasitic bee in the family Apidae, reported from warm parts of the Old World.
sections.identification: It has largely red legs and abdomen, with conspicuous pale hair spots along the rear abdominal segments.
sections.habitat: Its distribution is patchy in Europe; in Switzerland, records are concentrated in warm Valais habitats.
sections.diet: The sources consulted focus on nest parasitism and do not document this species’ adult diet.
sections.behavior: Females enter host nests and place eggs in brood cells; the first larval stage can kill the host offspring and competing cuckoo-bee larvae.
sections.reproduction: A detailed Pakistan study found its eggs and first instars in nests of Pseudapis diversipes, also called Nomiapis diversipes in some regional accounts.
sections.ecology: It exploits ground-nesting Nomiinae bees such as Pseudapis/Nomiapis diversipes; the host species digs clustered cells in branching underground tunnels.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted provide no global population assessment or Red List status for this bee.
